verdict.rationale: Zapier documents that outside developers can build integrations (Visual Builder or the Platform CLI) and publish them to the App Directory, which makes it a first-party channel for externally contributed connectors. The evidence describes the publishing side only; it does not show how a developer discovers, installs or vets a third-party integration. missing for 10: explicit docs on installing or using externally published integrations, community (non-vendor-partner) contribution and vetting model, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install community-built nodes, components, or integrations contributed outside the vendor

citations.quote: Build a Zapier integration - design triggers and actions for your product, wire up authentication, then publish to the App Directory.
Zapier Platform CLI enables developers to build integrations using Node.js v22, OAuth1/OAuth2 authentication, webhooks, polling triggers, and HTTP middleware.
Use the Visual Builder for quick, no-code setups or the CLI for full control and customization.
